$comment: The ONE canonical orchestration policy of the Udgam maths pipeline (every class). Read by orch.mjs (gates, plans, tiered checks, checkpoints), usage.mjs (budgets, simulate), classctl.mjs (each agent file's `model:` line and the escalated twins) and the cli.mjs hooks (check cache keys, runtime freeze gates). A class overrides any key in class<N>/pipeline.config.json under "orchestration" (deep merge: objects merge, arrays and scalars replace). Change a model here, then regenerate the agents: node classctl.mjs sync --from <M> --to <N> --only agents (dry run, then --apply on the owner's word). See udgam_maths_claude.md "Orchestration" and TOKENS.md.
principle: QUALITY FIRST, TOKENS SECOND (the owner, 2026-10-28, every class and chapter): no visual compromise, the best result, and every necessary check. Nothing that proves a tool is right is skipped, thinned or shortened to save tokens or time: the maths review of the final English, the language pass (tr-coverage), the FULL visual review (every frame of the review pack in English, Hindi and Gujarati), the play test where a tool is new or risky (real input), the image pass, and the final full check on 0 FAIL, then the upload audit for the chapter. Tokens are saved only by how the work is done: one chapter per session and contexts under 100k, reviewers working from the review pack, digests and check rows instead of whole sources, packs built once per round and re-looks on changed frames only, quick and cached checks before ONE full check, batched maths, language, image and audit work, reports of at most 40 lines, image reuse, Sonnet (no cap) for every look and Opus (5 at once) where it shortens the critical path.

models.$comment: Claude Code agent aliases (opus | sonnet | haiku | inherit) per role and stage. 'main' is advice for the session itself (/model), not a file. Opus where the result needs it: planning, every tool-builder (the builder agent files run on Opus, so the gate counts every builder as Opus and the 5-at-once cap really holds, the owner 2026-10-28), difficult maths, runtime work across tools, reviewer-conflict arbitration (routing below); Sonnet for every look (maths, language, visual, play, image), with no cap.

routing.$comment: Which tier a launch uses. 'escalated' = the <role>-escalated twin (models above). A follower builder starts on the base tier; it escalates only on a trigger. Since 2026-10-28 base and escalated builders both run on Opus (the agent files), so the tier only decides the reasons the gate asks for and the batch size.

limits.$comment: Per chapter build. A number is fixed; { base, perTool } is base + perTool x tools, rounded up; null = no cap. orch gate refuses a launch past a limit (exit 3). THE OWNER'S RULE (2026-10-28, every class and chapter): at most 5 OPUS agents RUNNING at once (maxConcurrentOpus), and NO cap on Sonnet or Haiku agents, as many as the chapter needs (maxConcurrent, maxAgentsPerChapter and maxReviewAgents are null). A class may set a number for any of them under pipeline.config.json orchestration.limits. chromeAdvisoryAt is not a limit: past that many builders and play testers running at once (each drives its own headless Chrome; more than 6 gave false timeouts on this machine, class 3 ch 9) the gate adds a note to its answer.

batching.$comment: Items per agent. orch plan picks the size (1..max) with the lowest modelled context cost that keeps every agent under contextBudget.targetTokens and the chapter under its agent limits.

contextBudget.$comment: Context is the cost driver (every call re-reads it). targetTokens: plan every agent under it. escalateTokens: a running agent past it is checkpointed and continued fresh, never resumed by SendMessage. Soft caps are what an agent can count itself.

checks.$comment: Tier 0 metadata, 1 quick (check --no-render), 2 one full check of a changed tool, 3 real-input play for new or risky interactions, 4 visual pack when visual changes justify it. A cached result is reused only when every key part matches.

review.$comment: Deduplication: maths on every tool (round 1), later rounds only where the maths digest changed; visual in FULL on every tool (every frame of the review pack in en, hi and gu: followerVisual is full since 2026-10-28, the owner: no visual compromise; light would bring back the reduced pass for a repeat of an unchanged pattern); play where a tool is new or risky; a re-review looks only at changed frames and named probes.

sprint.$comment: SPRINT MODE (runbook 'Sprint mode'; the owner, 2026-10-28: ONE tool fully ready in 40 minutes, where a normal build plus staged review took 1-2 hours, AND no review dropped: maths, the Gemini visual pass when kept, the language pass, the FULL visual review in en/hi/gu and the play tester all still run). Time comes from overlap and parallel agents, never from a skipped look. The clock: node orch.mjs sprint start|lap|status|stop. dueMin = minutes from the start; --minutes N scales them. What cost the hour in class 3 ch 9 was not the agents: it was owner decisions arriving after the builder started (photo or generated pictures, which objects, the start page, a new runtime rule), a checker row that failed on the machine (fixed in lib/core/chrome.mjs, 2026-10-28), a full check spent before the runtime pin, and every review waiting for the one before it. So a sprint needs every decision in ONE question before the builder; a decision after that is a line under 'after the sprint' in NOTES.md unless the owner restarts the clock.

stages.label: builder + image agent from minute 0; green quick check, <Skin> drawn. At the FIRST green quick check start, in parallel: the maths reviewer and the language draft agent (TR hi/gu into tr.draft.md from node orch.mjs digest --strings)
maths findings in and applied in ONE builder message (with the runtime freeze/pin if a gap is logged); a changed English line changes its TR draft line
builder merges the TR draft (language pass: tx in Work and Thumb, fit sheets), then ONE full check on the final pin and the final English

shots --pack ONCE (every frame, en + hi + gu); visual reviewers IN PARALLEL (one per language, or per 40-frame chunk: node orch.mjs chunks) and play testers IN PARALLEL (rows check already played, then split probes); all of it, all frames
every must-fix AND should-fix in ONE builder message, quick check, shots --pack --changed, the reviewers re-look ONLY at the changed frames (in parallel), the final full check (ports), status, report

designStage.label: Gemini visual pass (4b: node cli.mjs design, then the builder reads shots); after the maths fixes and the pin, before the merge of the TR draft (it never touches TR or the printed sentences, so the language draft is not redone)

sprint.designNote: The Gemini design pass is the OWNER'S choice, asked once in step 2 with its cost stated (sprint start --design adds designStage and its minutes to every later deadline and to the budget). It is never skipped silently and never cut when late.

parallel.visual: one reviewer per language (en, hi, gu) on the full pack, or per chunk of visualChunkFrames frames; each reports at most 40 lines
parallel.play: two play testers on the same tool: phases 1-2 and 3-4 (each with its own headless Chrome through playkit), the keyboard, classroom and Hindi/Gujarati probes split between them
parallel.translation: a language agent drafts hi/gu from the English strings as soon as the first quick check is green, in a scratch file; only changed lines are re-translated after the maths fixes
parallel.gateOver: launches beyond the normal agent caps pass --over "sprint: <role> <part>" to node orch.mjs gate; the cost is accepted by the owner

ifLate: start the next stage on the part that is already final
add parallel agents for the stage that is behind (gate --over sprint)
write what is open into NOTES.md and report the TRUE finish time; a review is never dropped to meet the clock
neverCut: the maths review of the final English
the Gemini visual pass when the owner kept it
the visual review of every frame in en, hi and gu
the final full check with 0 FAIL
the owner's decisions written down before the builder starts

opusAgents.complexWhen: the tool has an interaction in review.highRiskInteraction (a drag, two-box, fraction or decimal card, point key, card answer, an act, a narrow pad), a kind of picture no finished tool of the class has, or hard maths; otherwise simple. sprint start --complexity simple|complex sets it. Since 2026-10-28 (the owner: five Opus agents at a time) the standing cap, limits.maxConcurrentOpus, is already 5 for every build, so both figures are 5; orchlib/gate.mjs takes the HIGHER of the standing cap and the sprint's own, so a sprint can only lift the cap, never lower it (a figure below the standing one changes nothing)

limits.$comment: Read by orch gate while a sprint runs (state.sprint, not stopped) and laid over the standing limits. It holds no head-count or concurrency figure on purpose: the standing rule (5 Opus agents at once, no cap on Sonnet agents, the owner 2026-10-28) is already the most a sprint needs, and a figure here would re-cap Sonnet. The Opus figure is opusAgents above.

sprint.opusSlots: spend the Opus slots where they shorten the critical path, in this order: 1 the tool-builder; 2 the maths reviewer, escalated (the hard maths is what a wrong tool costs most); 3 a second builder, escalated, for the fold and the fix messages while the first builder keeps the tool moving; 4 and 5 the play tester and a visual reviewer on the riskiest parts (five Opus agents at once are standing since 2026-10-28, simple or complex). Sonnet agents do every other look and have no cap.
skip: second full-pack visual round (the re-look is --changed)

runtimeGates.$comment: Programmatic batching of runtime moves (runbook non-negotiable 3). `runtime freeze|pin` must name --ch N and --gate. prereview and postplay once each per chapter build; blocker only with --proof (a real-input probe), at most maxBlocker; step6 = a pin to the newest head at a chapter's own step 6. `freeze rN` (restore) is free; --ungated "why" is logged.

session.$comment: Session-limit guard. Claude Code does not expose the plan's percentage on disk, so orch gate uses the freshest of (a) the owner's reading (node orch.mjs session --pct 72, from /usage) and (b) a rolling-window estimate from local transcripts against budgetUsd5h (list-price-weighted; calibrate once: node usage.mjs window --calibrate <pct shown by /usage>). Unset budget and no reading = no session guard (the agent-count fallback, fallbackMaxAgentsPerWindow, is null since 2026-10-28 because the owner wants no cap on Sonnet agents; give it a number to bring it back).

estimates.$comment: The cost model of usage.mjs simulate (MODEL ASSUMPTIONS, not measurements: calibrate with `usage.mjs simulate --from <usage report.json>` once real transcripts exist). calls = model calls an agent makes; grow = tokens its context gains per call; start sizes are measured from the class's files.
